title: Maximum residue level for difenoconazole
summary: Updated EU MRLs for difenoconazole will apply from 5 May 2027 with a particular impact on watercresses …
update:
The European Union (EU) has updated the maximum residue levels (MRLs) for difenoconazole. For some products where there is not enough data available to rule out risks to consumers, the MRLs have been lowered to the limit of determination (LOD). (The LOD is the lowest level that can be detected using the most modern and reliable analytical methods.)

For other products, MRLs based on Codex Amimentarius MRLs have been set following an evaluation that raised no consumer safety concerns.

what_changing:
The EU has updated the MRLs for difenoconazole as summarised in Table 1.

For many of the products listed in Table 1 with MRLs above the LOD, the EU plans a further review within 2 years, as the available data on these products is currently limited.
why:
A series of assessments of difenoconazole residues were undertaken by the European Food Safety Authority ( EFSA 2024 , 2025 ).

MRLs were amended for the following reasons:

MRLs were maintained or lowered where there was sufficient supporting data on good agricultural practices and no risk for consumers was identified MRLs were set on the basis of Codex Alimentarius MRLs (CXLs) where no risk for consumers was identified when no information was available to allow risk assessment, MRLs were reduced to the LOD.
timeline: The new MRLs apply from 5 May 2027 .
actions: Exporters of all products should review their current use of difenoconazole to see whether agricultural practices need to be adjusted to comply with the updated MRLs. Where MRLs have been reduced to the LOD, exporters need to look for alternative solutions.
background: MRLs are set in accordance with the rules set out in Regulation 396/2005 . For information on current MRLs for other substances, please consult the EU Pesticide Residues database .
